task.title: Tabs and stock levels
task.html:
A jQuery course in 10 lessons.
Selectors, classes, events, AJAX.
"Clear from the very first lesson!"

Kits in stock

  • Notebook
  • Pen
  • USB stick
  • Stickers
  • Notepad
task.description: The page has three tabs .tab, three panels .panel (all with the class is-hidden) and a list of products li.product with the data-stock attribute - the number of items in stock. The classes is-active, is-hidden and is-low are already described in CSS. 1) Write the function setActiveTab(index): remove the class is-active from all .tab elements and set aria-selected="false" on them; add is-active and aria-selected="true" to the tab with the number index (with .eq); remove is-hidden from the panel with the number index and add it to all the others - with .toggleClass("is-hidden", state). 2) Write the function markLowStock(limit): add the class is-low to each .product whose data-stock is less than limit, and remove it from the others. Find the products inside the function. 3) At the end, call setActiveTab(0) and markLowStock(5). The tests call the functions many times with different arguments. Do not use document.querySelector, classList, .style, innerHTML or .html().

tests.name: The functions setActiveTab and markLowStock are declared
tests.fail: Declare both functions with the names from the task: function setActiveTab(index) { ... } and function markLowStock(limit) { ... }.

tests.name: After loading, the first tab is active and the first panel is visible
tests.fail: At the end of the code, call setActiveTab(0);

tests.name: setActiveTab(2): only the third tab is active
tests.fail: First $tabs.removeClass("is-active") on all of them, then $tabs.eq(index).addClass("is-active").

tests.name: setActiveTab(2): aria-selected="true" only on the third tab
tests.fail: Set .attr("aria-selected", "false") on all tabs and .attr("aria-selected", "true") on the needed one.

tests.name: setActiveTab(1): only the second panel is visible
tests.fail: Go through .panel with .each and call $(this).toggleClass("is-hidden", i !== index).

tests.name: Several switches in a row: 2, then 0
tests.fail: Each call must first remove the old state from all tabs and panels.

tests.name: A repeated call with the same number does not break anything
tests.fail: toggleClass without a second argument switches the class back and forth. Pass a state: .toggleClass("is-hidden", i !== index), or use addClass.

tests.name: The tab and panel classes are not lost
tests.fail: Do not overwrite the class attribute with .attr("class", ...) - use addClass / removeClass / toggleClass.

tests.name: markLowStock(5): is-low on the products with stock 3 and 0 (5 is not less than 5)
tests.fail: Use a strict comparison: stock < limit. Get the stock with $(this).data("stock").

tests.name: markLowStock(10) after markLowStock(5): 3, 0, 5 and 8 are marked
tests.fail: The function must work with any limit, not only with 5.

tests.name: markLowStock(1) removes extra marks
tests.fail: Products whose stock is not less than limit must lose the class is-low: .toggleClass("is-low", stock < limit).

tests.name: A product added after loading is checked too
tests.fail: Find the products inside the function: $(".product") on every call, not once at the start of the program.

tests.name: Classes are changed with jQuery methods
tests.fail: Use .eq(index) to select the tab and .toggleClass("name", state) for the panels or products.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Check the method names and make sure the functions are called after they are declared.

hints: Stock: $(this).data("stock") is already a number, so you can compare it with limit.
One call $(this).toggleClass("is-low", stock < limit) both adds and removes the class.
Do not forget to call both functions at the end of the program.

questions.question: What does $(".card").addClass("is-new") do if the cards already have the class card?
options: Replaces the class card with is-new
Adds is-new only to the first card
Nothing: an element can have only one class
questions.explanation: addClass adds a class to the existing ones, like classList.add, and does it on all the elements found.

questions.question: What happens after two calls in a row: $box.toggleClass("is-open"); $box.toggleClass("is-open"); (there was no class at first)?
options: The class is-open is not there
questions.explanation: Without a second argument, toggleClass switches: the first call added the class, the second removed it.

questions.question: What is the result of $box.toggleClass("is-open", true).toggleClass("is-open", true).hasClass("is-open")?
options: An error: hasClass cannot be used in a chain
questions.explanation: With the second argument true, toggleClass always adds the class, no matter how many times you call it. hasClass is a getter, it goes at the end of the chain and returns true.

questions.question: Which jQuery method returns true or false depending on whether the element has a class? Enter the method name without parentheses.
Which lines correctly remove the class is-hidden from the element $panel in jQuery 4?
questions.explanation: toggleClass(false) without a class name no longer works in jQuery 4, and css() works with CSS properties, not with classes.

questions.question: What does $("#box").css("color") return if CSS sets color: red for #box?
options: undefined, because the color is not set in the style attribute
questions.explanation: The css() getter returns the computed value that the browser applied to the element, even if it came from the CSS file. The browser returns colors in rgb() format.

questions.question: What does $("#title").css("font-size", 24) do in jQuery 4?
options: Changes nothing: a number without units is invalid for font-size
questions.explanation: In jQuery 4, px is added automatically only to sizes, margins and paddings, and positions (width, margin, top...). For font-size the browser ignores the value 24. That is why the course always writes units explicitly: "24px".

questions.question: Match the method with what it returns for a block: width 200px, padding 10px, border 2px, margin 5px (box-sizing: content-box).
questions.explanation: width is the content only, inner adds padding, outer also adds the border, and outerWidth(true) also adds margin.

questions.question: In which cases is .css() appropriate instead of a class?
options: A progress bar width calculated in code: 37%
Hide an error when the input is correct
The position of a tooltip at the cursor coordinates
Red color for an overdue task
questions.explanation: Values calculated in code are set with css(). States known in advance (hidden, error, overdue) are described with a class in CSS.

questions.question: How is .offset() different from .position()?
options: They are the same, these are synonyms
.offset() gives coordinates relative to the document, .position() relative to the nearest positioned parent
questions.explanation: Both return an object { top, left }, but they measure from different reference points.

questions.question: Complete the code that scrolls the page to the very top: $(window).______(0). Enter the method name without parentheses.
questions.explanation: scrollTop() without an argument reads the scroll position, and scrollTop(0) writes it.

questions.question: Match plain JavaScript code with jQuery code.
questions.explanation: jQuery does the same thing, but on all the elements found at once.
